model: Consolidated owner-FCF DCF (engine route) with Sumitomo Pharma minority deducted at market value in the equity bridge

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average 1,640,724k (basic 1,640,185k + 539k restricted stock), FY to 31-Mar-2026 EPS note; held FLAT -- SBC is immaterial and expensed, no convertibles, no equity raise planned (Note 2 to the EPS note: no significant share transactions after year end)
inputs.sbc_source: Annual FY to 31-Mar-2026, cash flow reconciliation line 'Share-based payment' 101 (restricted stock plan); no equity-award tax withholding line exists. Effectively an SBC-zero filer; the SBC row is kept explicit at 0% and house and street coincide
inputs.buyback_note: Purchase of treasury shares 6 (yen millions) in each of the last three years -- odd-lot buy-ins only, no repurchase programme. Recorded as 0.0
inputs.fy0_note: Metrics.csv labels fiscal years by their END year: CSV FY2026 = year ended 31-Mar-2026, which the company itself calls 'FY2025'. All driver years follow the CSV convention: Y1 = year ending 31-Mar-2027 = company 'FY2026' guidance year
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z regular TSE close (Friday); valuation date is the following Saturday
inputs.balance_sheet_note: The June-2026 Q1 report has not been extracted into this folder, so the March-2026 annual balance sheet is the latest available anchor (seven months old). The one known post-balance-date event that moves the bridge -- Sumitomo Pharma's April-2026 public offering -- is applied pro forma in equity_bridge. Refresh net debt and NCI from the Q1/H1 FY2026 tanshin when they are extracted
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. Cost of equity 8.5% = 10y JGB ~1.8% + beta 1.2 x ERP 5.5% (diversified chemicals with petrochemical and semiconductor-cycle exposure). After-tax cost of debt ~1.1% (Note 19: bonds 1.38%, long-term borrowings 1.00%, short-term 4.13% on foreign-currency lines; 30.6% statutory shield). Weighted at management's target structure (~80/20 after the disposal-funded deleveraging; D/E target below 0.7x) gives 7.0%. Market-value weights today (~65/35 on a 927bn market cap against 943bn net debt) would give ~5.9%, but current leverage is above management's own target and is being paid down from disposals, so target weights are used. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality, feedstock and pharma-pipeline risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities of 93,672 (31-Mar-2026, Note on other financial liabilities) are deducted once in equity_bridge; lease principal (20,643 in FY0 financing) is NOT deducted from the flows; EBITDA and D&A stay on the reported post-IFRS-16 basis; capex_pct_path carries ~0.5pp of revenue for right-of-use renewals (new lease additions ran 11-12bn/yr in the lease-liability roll-forward). total_debt 1,151,455 is bonds and borrowings only (Note 19) and ties to the Metrics.csv TotalDebt column
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge, not in the flows. Flows are 100% consolidated (Sumitomo Pharma remains a consolidated subsidiary after the April-2026 offering; Note 41 states the issuance 'will not result in any changes to the status of Sumitomo Pharma as a consolidated subsidiary'; SC's voting stake fell from 51.81% to 45.84%, de facto control). The 54.16% of Sumitomo Pharma not owned by SC is deducted at MARKET value (4506.T close) rather than book, because book NCI (141,086) is far below the stake's traded value and a book deduction would hand SC shareholders value that belongs to the minority. Other subsidiaries' NCI (86,943) is deducted at book. Modelled FY0 attributable check: core OI 208,376 less D&A-neutral items, less cash tax 27,379, less interest paid 29,833, less Pharma NCI share 51,551 lands near the reported attributable net income of 60,947 once the 105.8bn of business-transfer gains inside core OI are netted against 34.6bn impairments and 26.6bn restructuring -- i.e. the leakage is captured by the bridge, not double-charged. If SC ever loses control and Sumitomo Pharma becomes equity-accounted, SC's economic value is unchanged: its 45.84% stake would simply move from (consolidated flows minus NCI) to a bridge asset at the same market value
inputs.matching_asset_rule: Finance income (28,100 in FY0: interest 8,511, dividends on cross-shareholdings, FX) sits below operating income and is excluded from the EBITDA-based flows, so the source assets go into the bridge: FVOCI shares and investments 293,738 (marketable 121,179; non-marketable 172,559 of which Petro Rabigh Class B shares 99,192 at a level-3 fair value) plus FVTPL other financial assets 26,474, taken at fair value less a 20% haircut for tax on realization and illiquidity -- SC is an active seller (121bn of disposal proceeds in FY0, 180bn in FY-1) so these are real funding sources, not dead cross-holdings. Equity-method investments (203,862) are NOT added: their share of profit is inside core operating income (Note to the segment table: -43,271 in FY0, almost all Petro Rabigh in Essential & Green Materials) and therefore inside the flows. Interest income is not stripped (net-debt filer; rule only applies to net cash > 1x FCF)
inputs.flows_basis_note: EBITDA = core operating income + D&A (the company's own segment-profit measure, which excludes impairments, restructuring costs and disposal gains). Two consequences are handled explicitly: (1) FY0 core OI of 208,376 contains 105.8bn of business-transfer gains (55,807 in Essential & Green Materials, 50,024 in Sumitomo Pharma from the Asian pharma sale), so FY0 is NOT the margin anchor -- the FY1 guidance (core OI 215bn on 2,360bn revenue, which management says contains no comparable one-offs; underlying ~80bn FY-1 -> ~130bn FY0 -> ~210bn FY1) is. (2) Core OI excludes restructuring cash costs that have run 23.6bn and 26.6bn in the last two years (~1% of revenue) and are continuing (Keiyo Ethylene optimisation to end-FY2026, Singapore, Prime Polymer integration), so the base EBITDA path is set ~0.5pp below the guided 14.2% in years 1-3 rather than at it
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf is the reported consolidated FCF (OCF 234,759 less capex 121,566) less SBC 101. It is a LEVERED figure under SC's IFRS presentation (interest paid 29,833 is inside operating cash flow) and carries 26.6bn of restructuring cash costs and 27.4bn of cash tax on an NOL-sheltered base; the engine's unlevered component build produces ~140bn in Y1, and the gap is those three items. The flat share count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for through buybacks, but with SBC at 101 there is nothing to fund
inputs.notes: MODEL: consolidated owner-FCF DCF via the component engine, Sumitomo Pharma NCI deducted at market in the bridge. A sum-of-the-parts (ChemCo DCF + 45.84% listed stake at market) was considered and rejected only because Sumitomo Pharma's third-party interest-bearing debt is not separately disclosed in SC's filings (the IFRS 12 summarized balance sheet is pre-elimination and would include intercompany loans), so ChemCo net debt would rest on a +/-50bn estimate (~+/-30 yen/share); the market-NCI treatment reaches the same economics from disclosed numbers only. Pro forma check: pre-offering (48.24% NCI x pre-offering market cap, March-2026 cash) and post-offering (54.16% NCI, cash +97,842) bridges agree within 1bn because the offering was priced at market. ROUTING: operating company, non-US and cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency, leases, NCI, matching asset, SBC-zero, risk-once all applied). IFRS from CSV FY2018 (company FY2017); JGAAP years FY2016-FY2017 directional only. Yahoo 4005.T quotes JPY against JPY statements: no FX bridge. Sumitomo Pharma stake arithmetic: SC holds ~205.8m shares (51.81% voting of ~397.3m outstanding pre-offering; 45.84% of ~449.0m post the 51,304,400-share offering at 1,990 yen, Note 41), so the minority holds ~243.2m shares; at the 4506.T close of 1,884.5 yen on 2026-10-30 (52w range 1,188-3,288) the deduction is ~458.3bn. Every 100 yen move in 4506.T moves SC's value by ~15 yen/share. band_position is null: SBC-zero filer, house and street coincide

historical_growth.basis: IFRS era only (CSV FY2018 onward); 3yr = CSV FY2023->FY2026, 5yr = CSV FY2021->FY2026
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (101 or less every year; interest income not stripped, net-debt filer). 3yr is undefined: the CSV FY2023 base (-31,960) is negative. 5yr runs from the FY2021 peak (253,652, a working-capital release year) to 113,193
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: FY1 from company guidance (+1.4%), then 3.0-3.5% while Sumitomo Pharma's US franchise and the agro/semiconductor-materials pipeline scale, fading to 2.0%; equity CAGR is unusable as a growth anchor because the FY2023 record loss (CSV FY2024: -311,838 attributable) sits inside both windows
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-4.9% 3yr) diverges from EPS CAGR (+105.8% 3yr, off a 4.27 yen base) by far more than 30%; both are artefacts of the FY2023 trough. Revenue is shrinking by design (-7.0% 3yr) as petrochemical capacity is rationalised, so revenue CAGR understates the earnings trajectory. None of the three is a usable anchor; the base path is anchored to guidance and the mid-cycle core-EBITDA margin history instead
historical_growth.notes: Consolidated core EBITDA margin (core OI + D&A) by CSV year: FY2018 16.9%, FY2019 13.7%, FY2020 11.9%, FY2021 12.4%, FY2022 14.2%, FY2023 9.0%, FY2024 0.3%, FY2025 10.4%, FY2026 14.1% (10.8% ex the 105.8bn of disposal gains). Mid-cycle ex the FY2023-24 crisis is ~12.5-13.5%; the FY1 guided 14.2% sits at the top of that range but on a portfolio with materially less commodity petrochemical weight (Essential & Green Materials 29% of FY0 revenue vs Essential Chemicals 35-40% in FY2016-19) and a larger, recovering pharma franchise

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = guidance 2,360bn (+1.4%: Sumitomo Pharma +19.5%, Agro +7.8%, ICT +2.8%, Essential & Green Materials -17.5% from restructuring). Y2-5 3.0-3.5% as the E&GM shrinkage ends and pharma/agro/semiconductor materials grow mid-single digits; fade to 2.0% (JPY nominal, mature chemicals)
base.margin_rationale: Guided FY1 core EBITDA margin is 14.2% (core OI 215 + D&A 121 on 2,360). Base starts 0.5pp below it to carry continuing restructuring cash costs that core OI excludes, then rises to 14.5% by Y5 as mix shifts to Agro and ICT (growth-driver share of core OI 56% in FY1 guidance vs 29% in FY2017) -- 1pp above the ex-crisis mid-cycle, justified by the smaller commodity base, and held flat thereafter
base.capex_rationale: Guided FY1 capex 119bn (5.0% of revenue) plus ~0.5pp of right-of-use lease renewals under treatment A; 5.6% in Y1-2 covers the heavier front half of the 450bn FY2025-27 capex/loans/investments plan, easing to 5.3% (modestly above D&A at 5.0% for ~2% growth)
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax ramps 24% -> 29%: FY0 cash tax was 27.4bn on 116bn pre-tax (23.6%) with NOLs from the FY2023 loss; mature rate held 1.6pp below the 30.6% Japanese statutory rate for Sumitomo Pharma's US loss carryforwards and overseas mix
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables 608.7 + inventories 595.5 - payables 464.4 = 739.8bn, 32% of revenue; growth consumes cash at -25% of the revenue change (inventories were being run down in FY0, so the capture is set below the balance-sheet ratio)
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 13x FCF (cyclical, 12-15x house range) binds against a 7%/1% Gordon of 16.8x; the implied terminal EV/EBITDA is ~5.3x against SC's own 6-9x trading history, i.e. no re-rating is assumed
base.narrative: Restructuring largely done; the portfolio delivers the guided FY1 and compounds modestly without a petrochemical re-rating

bull.narrative: Guidance beaten on all three growth drivers at once; margins reach the FY2018 peak level of ~16-17% on a better mix; capex runs higher to fund it

bear.narrative: Guidance missed on naphtha and a Y2-3 petrochemical/semiconductor downcycle; margins revisit the FY2019-21 trough band (~11-12%); maintenance-only capex; a 1% lower terminal cap for a company that does not shed its cyclicality

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2023 crisis is behind the company: the 10% headcount cut, the Petro Rabigh and Asian-pharma disposals and the Keiyo/Singapore rationalisations have shrunk the commodity base, and FY1 guidance (sales 2,360bn, core OI 215bn, net income 70bn at 155 yen/USD and 92,000 yen/kl naphtha) is delivered within ~0.5pp of margin. Sumitomo Pharma's US franchise (Orgovyx, Gemtesa, Rethymic) grows ~20% in Y1 and mid-single digits after; Agro & Life Solutions scales biorationals and the first of the three in-house actives; ICT & Mobility rides the AI-driven photoresist and high-purity chemicals cycle with the AUECC bolt-on. Core EBITDA margin rises from 13.7% to 14.5% and stays there -- one point above the ex-crisis mid-cycle, reflecting the smaller petrochemical weight, not a structural re-rating. The cash tax rate normalises as NOLs are consumed, capex runs modestly above D&A, and the terminal value is capped at 13x FCF (~5.3x EBITDA). Risk is carried in the 30% bear weight and the flows, not in a WACC premium.
scenario_narratives.bull: All three growth engines land together: Amchepry (iPS-cell Parkinson's therapy, conditional approval March 2026) converts to the >100bn-yen franchise management describes, the INDIFLIN/Rapidicil/Pavecto agro actives ramp toward their tens-of-billions targets by the early 2030s, and the High-NA EUV / advanced-packaging materials cycle persists so ICT & Mobility compounds high-single digits. Naphtha relief and the Prime Polymer integration lift Essential & Green Materials above its 20bn guidance. Consolidated core EBITDA margin returns to the ~16% FY2018 peak on a far better mix, revenue compounds 5-6% in Y2-4, and the exit is a 15x FCF cap with 1.5% terminal growth. Capex is held higher (6%) because this outcome has to be paid for.
scenario_narratives.bear: The guided FY1 is missed: the 92,000 yen/kl naphtha assumption proves too low or Middle East supply disruption (Singapore force majeure, March 2026) stretches into lost volume that cannot be passed through; a Y2-3 Asian petrochemical and memory/logic capex downcycle pushes the consolidated core EBITDA margin back to the 11-12% FY2019-21 band; Sumitomo Pharma's US pricing and the post-marketing conditions on Amchepry (full approval contingent on studies through FY2032) cap its contribution; and the equity-method and FX finance-expense swings that have hit the P&L repeatedly recur. Revenue is flat for two years and then grows 1.5%. With net debt plus leases at ~3x guided EBITDA and a covenant breach on record (long-term borrowings reclassified to current at 31-Mar-2026), the bear case is not a solvency case but it is a case where SC shareholders see little of the group's cash. Terminal cap 11x, 0.5% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: leverage (net debt plus leases ~3x guided EBITDA, after a covenant breach and a 110bn-yen intercompany debt waiver inside the last two years), a commodity segment the company cannot cost-compete in structurally, guidance built on a sharply higher naphtha price, unhedged medium-term FX, and minority leakage that rises when the most profitable subsidiary does well. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (a first-in-class cell therapy commercialising, three agro actives ramping, and a semiconductor materials cycle persisting) plus naphtha relief. Base 50%: FY1 guidance is management's own, and the last two years were delivered or beaten.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the consolidated cash flows of a restructured, still-leveraged, still-cyclical chemicals group at a JPY cost of capital, deduct every claim ahead of SC shareholders exactly once (bonds and borrowings, IFRS 16 leases, the 54% of Sumitomo Pharma owned by the public at what the market pays for it, other minorities at book) and add back the investment securities whose dividends were excluded from the flows. Capping the terminal at 13x FCF (~5x EBITDA) means the model pays nothing for a re-rating of a company that has traded at 6-9x EBITDA for a decade; the probability weights, not the discount rate, carry the cyclicality. The reading is that the stock trades close to the probability-weighted value: the market is already pricing the recovery management has guided, and the 15% hurdle entry price sits well below the current price, as it does for any slow compounder discounted at 7%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Sumitomo Pharma's share price is the largest single swing factor outside the flows: the minority deduction is marked to 4506.T (52-week range 1,188-3,288 yen), and every 100 yen move is ~15 yen per SC share

Guidance rests on 92,000 yen/kl naphtha and 155 yen/USD; the petrochemical segment's 20bn guided core OI is the residual after feedstock pass-through, and Middle East supply risk is explicitly unquantified by management

Core operating income excludes restructuring cash costs (~1% of revenue in each of the last two years) and impairments; a base margin path 0.5pp below guidance is the only allowance made for their continuation

Leverage: net debt plus leases of ~1,037bn against guided EBITDA of 336bn; long-term borrowings in covenant conflict were reclassified to current at 31-Mar-2026 and the Sumitomo Pharma guarantees were only released in April 2026 -- a second earnings shock would hit equity holders disproportionately
The 20% haircut on 320bn of investment securities and the level-3 mark on Petro Rabigh Class B shares (99bn) are judgments; a 40% haircut would remove ~40 yen per share
The March-2026 balance sheet is seven months old; the June-2026 quarter has not been extracted, so net debt, NCI and working capital should be refreshed on the next update

Sumitomo Pharma deconsolidation: value-neutral in this bridge by construction, but it would change every reported consolidated metric the sanity check reads (revenue, EBITDA, net debt) and must be re-based if it happens
